scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #9027: After a maintenance window, routes for the R7 region (17.x.x.x,
67.0.0.0/8, 70.0.0.0/8) vanished from R1's routing table and R6 lost its OSPF
neighbor R7. The team believes the R6<->R7 link (67.0.0.0/8) went down or was
unplugged during the maintenance. Please confirm the R6<->R7 link failure and
identify the down interface.

injection.action: kill ospfd (kill watchfrr first so FRR does not respawn it)

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath5-r7-ospfd-down: ospfd is dead on R7. With its
ospfd stopped, R6 ages out R7's LSAs and the withdrawals propagate through area 1
and the backbone, so R1 loses the R7 region (17.x, 67.x, 70.x).

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- a downed R6<->R7 link
(67.0.0.0/8). The link is actually UP and forwarding (R6 and R7 can still reach
each other's 67.x interface IPs); nothing physical failed. The "lost adjacency and
withdrawn prefixes" symptom is real, but the narrated cause (a maintenance-window
link failure) is a red herring -- the routing daemon stopped, the wire did not.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = r7 (ospfd not running). The
agent must check Layer 1/2 (the R6<->R7 link / 67.x interfaces are up), then the
routing daemon (ospfd dead on R7), and explicitly reject the "link down"
narrative. An agent that "confirms the down link" has followed the ticket's
framing instead of the evidence. Fix: `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on R7.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r7" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the ospfd daemon on r7 (e.g. `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on
r7). Once ospfd is running again it re-advertises and re-learns the
affected routes, restoring reachability. (The ticket misattributes the fault;
the remediation targets r7.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on R7: the OSPF daemon (`ospfd`) is not running. The physical R6–R7 link (segment Y, 67.0.0.0/8) is fully intact — both R6 eth2 (67.1.1.1/8) and R7 eth0 (67.1.1.2/8) show `UP/LOWER_UP` with bidirectional traffic counters. The link was not unplugged.

The mechanism is a dead control-plane process, not a dead data-plane link. With `ospfd` absent on R7, R7 never sends OSPF hellos on eth0. R6's OSPF process on eth2 remains DR with Neighbor Count = 0, waiting indefinitely. Because R7 originates the only LSAs for its loopbacks (17.1.1.1–17.1.4.1/24) and its stub network (70.0.0.0/8, eth1 = segment AA), those prefixes vanish from the OSPF LSDB and consequently from every downstream router including R1. R1 still retains 67.0.0.0/8 because R6 independently advertises it as a directly connected network; the ticket's claim that 67.0.0.0/8 "vanished" from R1 is inaccurate — only the R7-originated prefixes (17.x.x.x and 70.0.0.0/8) are missing.

The `ospfd=yes` line in R7's `/etc/frr/daemons` and the complete OSPF stanzas in `/etc/frr/frr.conf` (router-id 67.1.1.2, all four `network` statements) confirm the configuration is correct and intact. The daemon was stopped or killed during the maintenance window and never restarted.

Root cause: `ospfd` was stopped on R7 during the maintenance window and was not brought back up.

Corrective fix: Restart the FRR OSPF daemon on R7 — run `service frr restart` (or `/usr/lib/frr/frrinit.sh restart`) on R7. Once ospfd starts, it will load frr.conf, form adjacency with R6 on eth2, flood its LSAs, and R1 will recover 17.x.x.x and 70.0.0.0/8 within one OSPF convergence cycle.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names the OSPF routing daemon (ospfd) as not running on R7, satisfying the requirement to identify the component.
The agent recommends restarting the FRR/ospfd daemon on R7 (e.g., service frr restart), which matches the expected remediation to restore OSPF and re-advertise the missing routes.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations (interfaces up on both sides, ospfd absent from R7 process list, daemons file and frr.conf present) that support the conclusion; inferences about adjacency loss and withdrawn LSAs follow logically. A minor ungrounded detail (exact preservation of 67.0.0.0/8 on R1 and timing claim about the maintenance window) does not undermine the core diagnosis or remediation.
